detailed_rationale:
Afcons Infrastructure, the Shapoorji Pallonji group's EPC flagship, has genuine niche expertise in marine works, tunneling, and metro construction, and carries a large order book (Rs 32,496 crore as of March 2026, roughly 3x annual revenue) that provides multi-year revenue visibility. Full-year FY26 was still profitable -- EBITDA of Rs 14.39 bn (11.7% margin) and PAT of Rs 2.51 bn -- but Q4 FY26 was genuinely weak: revenue fell 18.9% YoY to Rs 2,613.84 crore, EBITDA margin narrowed sharply to 6.1% from 12.2% in the year-ago quarter, and the quarter closed with a net loss of roughly Rs 88-89 crore, which management attributed in part to macroeconomic uncertainty and unspecified one-time factors. I have not been able to independently verify the exact composition of those one-time items, so I am not crediting them at face value, but the margin collapse itself (more than halved YoY) is too large to be explained by one-offs alone.

A second concern beyond the Q4 print is the pace of order replenishment: full-year order inflows of Rs 4,125 crore versus a Rs 32,496 crore closing order book (roughly 13% book replenishment for the year) is modest relative to the scale of the backlog, and worth watching for whether the order book, while large, is being refreshed quickly enough to sustain the current revenue run-rate multiple years out. On capital efficiency, ROE (11.4%) and ROCE (20.9%) are genuinely respectable for an EPC business, and leverage (debt/equity 0.67x, interest coverage 1.84x) is moderate rather than alarming -- this is not a distressed balance sheet, it is a margin-volatility and order-inflow-pace story.
recommendation_rationale: The quant score is Sell on both horizons, and unlike some other names in this batch, the 1-year score (21.27) is actually slightly weaker than the 3-year score (23.18) -- there is no quant-recognized recent improvement to lean on here. Combined with a genuine Q4 margin collapse and modest order-inflow replenishment against a large backlog, I do not see a basis to override the quant Sell, notwithstanding respectable ROE/ROCE and a strong order book.
summary: Afcons Infrastructure is a large EPC contractor (Shapoorji Pallonji group) specializing in marine, tunneling, and metro construction, with a big order book that gives good revenue visibility. The full year was still profitable, but the most recent quarter was notably weak -- revenue fell and operating margins roughly halved -- and the pace at which new orders are replacing completed work has slowed relative to the size of the backlog. The balance sheet itself is not a concern, but the recent margin volatility is.
positive_para: The order book of Rs 32,496 crore (about 3x annual revenue) provides real multi-year revenue visibility, and full-year capital efficiency remains respectable (ROE 11.4%, ROCE 20.9%) with only moderate leverage (debt/equity 0.67x). Afcons has genuine execution expertise in higher-barrier niches (marine works, tunneling, metro) that differentiate it from generic roads-EPC players.
negative_para: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 18.9% YoY and EBITDA margin nearly halved (12.2% to 6.1%), resulting in a quarterly net loss -- a magnitude of margin volatility that is not fully explained by the unspecified one-time factors management cited. Full-year order inflows (Rs 4,125 crore) replaced only a modest share of the existing order book, raising a real question about whether backlog is being refreshed quickly enough, and the quant model's own 1-year score is, if anything, slightly weaker than its 3-year score -- there is no data-driven signal of recent improvement to lean on.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At a trailing PE near 42x, the market is paying a growth-infrastructure multiple for a company whose most recent quarter showed a sharp margin contraction and a net loss. Respectable full-year ROCE (20.9%) supports a reasonable multiple in a normal quarter, but the Q4 volatility and modest order-inflow replenishment make it hard to call the current price cheap -- this reads as a name where the order book supports the story but the last quarter's execution does not yet confirm it.
